trigger: list_pending_approvals/get_pending_approval_count (MCP) and GET /api/v1/approvals{,/pending/count} (REST) answered EVERY approval-store read failure -- including a PERMANENT one (schema drift, disk-full, store never opened, SQLSTATE class 42/53/25/XX) -- with the same transient retry_after_ms:5000 hint an actual pool-exhaustion failure gets.
summary: Derived HIGH (I4 harmful machine-actionable guidance -- an agentic caller told to retry a condition that will not clear, plus a wasted audit-write per retry attempt) + E3 (any authenticated Approval:Read caller, default config) -> BLOCKING, matching the reporter's own 'important' tally. Fixed by classifying via sqlstate/is_open() (mirroring the already-shipped ticket-consume path's mcp::approval_store_error_body): new mcp::approval_store_read_error_body (mcp_approval_error.hpp) for the two MCP tools, new detail::approval_store_error_json (rest_api_v1.cpp) for the two REST routes -- deliberately NOT reusing the ticket-consume function's wording verbatim, since list/count reads never name a ticket. Regression-tested both directions: DROP TABLE (42P01, permanent) and a lock_timeout-forced 55P03 (transient) now produce the correct message/retry_after_ms at all four call sites (two DROP TABLE MCP tests, two DROP TABLE REST tests updated; one new lock-timeout MCP test added per cpp-safety's SHOULD below).
classification_rationale: the pre-fix code had exactly one branch for every store-read failure, silently treating a permanent condition as retryable

classification_rationale: a missing test for a behaviour with bounded blast radius is SHOULD, not a policy floor
